title: The Conceptual Void: Why the AI Safety Taxonomy of Rights, Safety, and Security is Absurd
description: This article critically reviews the foundational taxonomy guiding proposed General-Purpose AI (GPAI) incident reporting systems, specifically the separation of "Rights," "Safety," and "Security" incidents. We argue that this framework is conceptually void and leads to a fundamental category error in governance. This framework further risks transforming liability regimes for human conduct into arbitrary permission regimes for technology, leading to governance based on narrative fear and speculative agency risks (e.g., "evasion of human control") rather than on demonstrable risk and legal principles. The resulting framework substitutes procedural compliance for substantive accountability and represents a critical deficit in conceptual competence within AI governance. We also raise questions about how this paper contribute to preserving scientific integrity, the stated purpose of the RAND Corporation and we argue it fails to do that.
